meaning.long_meaning: Aashutosh corresponds to the Sanskrit form आशुतोष. Its core lexical sense is quickly pleased (epithet of shiva). आशुतोष (Āśutoṣa) is an epithet of Shiva, 'who is quickly pleased'.

seo.description_paragraph: The name Aashutosh corresponds to the Sanskrit form आशुतोष, whose core lexical sense is quickly pleased (epithet of shiva). आशुतोष (Āśutoṣa) is an epithet of Shiva, 'who is quickly pleased'.

faq.a: Aashutosh corresponds to the Sanskrit form आशुतोष, whose core lexical sense is quickly pleased (epithet of shiva).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aashutosh?
faq.a: Aashutosh is associated with Sanskrit. आशुतोष (Āśutoṣa) is an epithet of Shiva, 'who is quickly pleased'.
Yes — the underlying form आशुतोष is Sanskrit.
Aashutosh is used in Hindu naming practice, but Sanskrit origin alone does not make a name Hindu. The classification here rests on documented naming usage.

faq.q: Is Aashutosh mentioned in the Vedas?
faq.a: No occurrence of this exact form in the Vedic corpus was verified. Absence of verification is not a claim of absence.

faq.q: How is Aashutosh written in Indian scripts?
faq.a: Sanskrit आशुतोष, Hindi आशुतोष, Marathi आशुतोष, Bengali আশুতোষ, Tamil ஆசுதோஷ், Telugu ఆశుతోష్.
A romanized syllable approximation is aas-hu-tosh. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: Is Aashutosh a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
